title: Keyboard mute for the MV7: mv7mute + Raycast + Hyper+M
description:
Goal: one key on the maintainer's ZSA Moonlander toggles the Shure MV7's own (hardware) mute, the same state the touch pad changes, with the mute LED following.

Chain: Moonlander key (Oryx) sends Hyper+M (Cmd+Ctrl+Opt+Shift+M) -> Raycast script command bound to Hyper+M -> runs the locally built `mv7mute` binary -> HID text command `micMute on|off` on interface 3 of the MV7 (14ed:1012).

The binary is built from source from the maintainer's fork (johndturn/mv7mute) after a security review (docs/security-review.md). Two review findings must be fixed before the tool is used on the mic: drop `bootDSP C` from init and open the HID device non-exclusively on macOS.

Done when: pressing the key mutes/unmutes within a fraction of a second, the LED follows, MOTIV settings are untouched, and it works with MOTIV Mix running or closed.

title: Stop restarting the DSP on every run (drop bootDSP C from init)
description:
Every invocation runs Mv7::init (mv7mute-core/src/mv7.rs), which sends `su adm` then `bootDSP C` and waits up to 5 s for `dspBooted`. The protocol write-up (schlarpc/shure-mv7-firmware-re, hid-protocol.md, command 8) describes bootDSP as "Start the DSP again with the default data" (level dev). Restarting the DSP on every key press risks an audible dropout and may reset the DSP settings the maintainer set in MOTIV Mix. mv7config only sends it once when its GUI starts; the mute command (micMute, level nor) does not need it.

Fix: remove the bootDSP step from init. Keep `su adm` (power-on level is already adm; `lock` needs adm).

If hardware testing shows micMute does NOT work without bootDSP, STOP and report to the maintainer. Do not quietly put it back.
acceptance_criteria: Mv7::init no longer sends bootDSP C or waits for dspBooted; unit tests (mv7mute-core/src/tests) updated to the new command sequence and passing; README How It Works / protocol table updated; cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings and test pass. Hardware check in the validation task confirms micMute works without it.
close_reason: bootDSP removed from init; mock tests and allowlist test pass; hardware check (.3) confirmed micMute works without it, no dropout, MOTIV settings unchanged.

title: An interrupted run can leave the settings lock off
description: If the mic's settings lock is on, init turns it off and Drop turns it back on. If the process is killed in between, the lock stays off. Only matters if the maintainer uses the lock (hold Mute + Monitor for 2 s).
acceptance_criteria: Decide: accept and document, or restore the lock on SIGINT/SIGTERM; decision noted here.

title: Offer the two fixes upstream as PRs to Justkant/mv7mute
description: The bootDSP removal and macOS shared-device fixes help every macOS user. Opening PRs on someone else's repo is outward-facing: only with the maintainer's explicit go-ahead, and keep the PR scoped to the fix (no AGENTS.md, .claude/, .beads/ files).
acceptance_criteria: After hardware validation passes, the maintainer approves; PRs opened against Justkant/mv7mute from branches on johndturn/mv7mute with the reasoning and test notes; links recorded here.

title: See mute state at a glance (menu bar or Moonlander LED)
description: Backlog idea. The MV7 LED shows mute, but it may be out of sight. Options: a Raycast menu-bar command polling `mv7mute status`; a tiny always-on listener for the micMute=... events; or a Moonlander LED via Keymapp/ZSA's API. Polling HID every few seconds would need the shared-open fix.
acceptance_criteria: Options compared and a choice made with the maintainer before any build.

title: CI: lint only on GitHub (fmt + clippy on Linux); tests and builds local
description: Hosted macOS runners do not pick up jobs on the fork's account (the macos-26 job on PR #1 was cancelled unacquired), and the maintainer does not want to spend Actions minutes on builds: there is no reason for this personal fork to build on Windows, and all builds and tests run locally (/verify on macOS, the only platform the mic is used on). Decision: GitHub runs lint and static analysis only.
acceptance_criteria: ci.yml: one ubuntu-latest job, cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy -D warnings on mv7mute-core and mv7mute only (no test or build matrix), pull_request only with a path filter on Rust/Cargo files, concurrency cancel-in-progress, timeout; AGENTS.md, docs/SDLC.md and /sync-upstream (keep the fork's ci.yml on conflict) updated; the lint job passes on the PR.
close_reason: ci.yml is lint only: fmt + clippy on the CLI crates, ubuntu-latest, PRs touching Rust/Cargo files. First run passed in about 16 s. Tests and builds are local (/verify).

title: Narrow the Bash guard hook to command positions (false positives on quoted text)
description: The PreToolUse guard (.claude/hooks/guard-bash.sh) greps the whole Bash command string, so it blocks harmless commands whose quoted text contains a blocked word: a commit message naming upstream's release tool, or a JSON fixture used to test the hook itself. Also, the TUI check anchors on end-of-line, and grep is line-based, so any line of a multi-line command ending in that word trips it. Workaround today: put long text in a file (git commit -F, gh pr create --body-file). Fix idea: strip quoted strings and heredoc bodies before matching, or split the command into simple commands with a real shell tokenizer (python3 shlex) and match argv. Must stay fail-closed when parsing fails.
acceptance_criteria: Blocked words inside quoted strings, heredocs and commit or PR message text no longer trip the hook; every real case still blocks (upstream push, publish, tag push, force-push of main, hook bypass, the bare TUI, gh pr create aimed at the parent repo); a fixture-driven test script asserts the exit code for each case; shellcheck clean.

title: Stop prompting for push, merge, rebase, reset and PR create/merge
description: The maintainer removed git push, git merge, git rebase, git reset, gh pr create and gh pr merge from the ask list in .claude/settings.json, to cut permission prompts during the PR loop. The deny rules and the guard hook (.claude/hooks/guard-bash.sh) still block force pushes, pushes or PRs aimed at the parent repo, tag pushes and hook bypass, and the git hooks still run the privacy scan. Merging stays the maintainer's call by process (docs/SDLC.md), not by prompt.
acceptance_criteria: settings.json ask list no longer has those six entries; deny rules and guard hook unchanged; AGENTS.md describes the settings accurately.
close_reason: Ask list trimmed by the maintainer; AGENTS.md updated.

title: mv7mute version prints the core crate's version, not the CLI's
description: Pre-existing upstream quirk: the version subcommand is answered in mv7mute-core (lib.rs, Command::Version) with env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"), which is mv7mute-core's version (0.1.1), while clap's --version prints the CLI crate's (0.1.3). Harmless; the installed build is identified by the fork commit recorded in AGENTS.md. A fix would pass the CLI's version in from mv7mute/src/main.rs; worth offering upstream (see .11) rather than diverging.
acceptance_criteria: mv7mute version and mv7mute --version print the same (CLI) version; the existing version test updated; no device I/O for version.

title: Open the MV7 HID device non-exclusively on macOS (hidapi macos-shared-device)
description:
hidapi's vendored macOS backend opens devices with kIOHIDOptionsTypeSeizeDevice (exclusive) unless the Rust crate's `macos-shared-device` feature is on (hidapi-2.6.5 src/lib.rs calls hid_darwin_set_open_exclusive(0) only under that feature). mv7mute-core depends on hidapi with default features, so on macOS it seizes interface 3. With MOTIV Mix running this either fails to open or cuts MOTIV off for the duration. The upstream README's "coexists with MOTIV" note is about Windows only.

Fix: enable the feature on macOS, e.g. in mv7mute-core/Cargo.toml:
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
hidapi = { version = "2.6.5", features = ["macos-shared-device"] }
(verify how Cargo merges this with the base dependency; keep the version in one place if possible).
acceptance_criteria: mv7mute-core enables hidapi's macos-shared-device feature for macOS targets only (target-specific dependency or feature), Cargo.lock updated with --locked builds still passing; Linux/Windows feature sets unchanged (cargo tree -e features shows it); clippy/test pass. Hardware check: mv7mute works while MOTIV Mix is running and MOTIV keeps working.
notes: Hardware checks for .3 (shared open): (1) with MOTIV Mix running, then launched after a run, then closed: status and toggle open the device without an exclusive-access error (0xE00002C5); (2) MOTIV stays connected and shows the mute change within ~1 s; (3) with MOTIV open, alternate toggle and status: status always matches the LED (no cross-talk misreads: replies to MOTIV's queries now reach us too); (4) mute from MOTIV's UI and from the pad, then status matches; (5) after the toggles, change a MOTIV setting and confirm it applies (shared su level / lock flip don't break MOTIV); lock back on if it was on; (6) no macOS permission prompt from Terminal (and later Raycast); (7) if MOTIV seizes the device so our open fails, stop and record it, do not fall back to exclusive mode. Cargo.lock does not record features, so it is correctly unchanged.
close_reason: macos-shared-device enabled for macOS only (Cargo.lock unchanged: it does not record features); hardware check (.3) confirmed the CLI and MOTIV Mix work side by side with correct state in both.

title: Validate on the real MV7 (maintainer watching the mic)
description:
Needs the maintainer present: the agent runs commands, the maintainer watches the mic's LED and listens. Run only the CLI's own subcommands (status, toggle, on, off). Do not send any other HID commands to the mic (see AGENTS.md "Hardware safety").

Before the first run, ask the maintainer to note the current MOTIV Mix settings (mode, EQ, limiter/compressor, gain) so (4) can be checked.

Measure latency with: /usr/bin/time -p ./target/release/mv7mute toggle (or hyperfine if installed; never more than ~10 toggles in a row).
acceptance_criteria: With a debug or release build of the patched CLI, the maintainer confirms and the results are recorded as a note on this issue: (1) mv7mute status matches the LED; (2) toggle/on/off flip the mute LED; (3) touching the pad then running status reports the new state; (4) a MOTIV setting (e.g. mode or EQ) is unchanged after 10 toggles; (5) no audible dropout while recording/monitoring during toggles; (6) works with MOTIV Mix open and closed, and MOTIV still shows correct state; (7) wall-clock time of one toggle measured (target < 300 ms).
notes:
Hardware check 2026-11-24, MV7 firmware 1.2.19.0, combined local build of the .1 (eee7c59) and .2 (7e22134) branches (release, --locked). 13 CLI runs (9 state-changing, 4 status), one at a time, maintainer watching the LED and monitoring through headphones on the mic. MOTIV Mix settings before: Manual, Monitor Mix 50%, gain +30 dB, EQ high-pass, limiter off, compressor Light.
MOTIV closed: status matched LED (unmuted/unlocked); toggle -> muted, toggle -> unmuted; pad tap then status -> muted; off -> unmuted; on -> muted; off -> unmuted. All LED changes and voice cut/return confirmed; no pop or dropout.
Then MOTIV opened: all settings unchanged after the 7 runs (no DSP reset). MOTIV open: status opened the device with no error and MOTIV stayed connected; toggle -> muted, MOTIV updated almost instantly; unmute from MOTIV's UI then status -> unmuted; pad tap (MOTIV showed muted) then status -> muted; toggle -> unmuted. A MOTIV setting changed afterwards applied normally (then restored). No macOS permission prompt.
Timing: 0.03-0.17 s wall clock per run (/usr/bin/time -p; first run 0.17 s, then 0.03-0.04 s). Target < 300 ms met.
Result: acceptance (1)-(7) all pass. micMute works without bootDSP; shared open coexists with MOTIV Mix on macOS.
close_reason: All 7 acceptance checks passed on the real MV7 with MOTIV open and closed; details in notes.

title: Build the CLI from source and install it on PATH
description:
Only the CLI crate is built and installed; the tray app (mv7mute-tray) is not used. Build only from a reviewed commit on the fork's main (after the P1 fixes are merged). Use --locked so Cargo.lock is honoured.

Raycast runs scripts with a minimal PATH, so the Raycast script must call the binary by absolute path; pick the path here.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build --release --locked -p mv7mute succeeds from a clean tree on the fork's main; binary installed at a stable absolute path (e.g. ~/.local/bin/mv7mute or ~/.cargo/bin/mv7mute via cargo install --path mv7mute --locked); mv7mute version prints the expected version; the chosen path and the commit it was built from are recorded in AGENTS.md (Local install section).
close_reason: Built with cargo build --release --locked -p mv7mute from a clean tree at fork main 53ba1f3; installed to ~/.local/bin/mv7mute (on PATH, arm64, checksum matches the build); mv7mute --version prints 0.1.3. Recorded in AGENTS.md Local install. Version subcommand quirk filed as .16.

title: Raycast script command: toggle MV7 mute (bound to Hyper+M)
description:
Raycast script commands are shell scripts with comment metadata (# @raycast.schemaVersion 1, # @raycast.title, # @raycast.mode silent, ...). In silent mode the last line of output is shown as a HUD. The hotkey is assigned in Raycast settings (Extensions > Script Commands), not in the script. Hyper = Cmd+Ctrl+Opt+Shift; check Raycast's own Hyper Key setting and existing Hyper+M bindings for conflicts.

Keep the script tiny: run `mv7mute toggle`, map its stdout (muted/unmuted) to the HUD text.
acceptance_criteria: Script at integrations/raycast/mv7-toggle-mute.sh (executable, shellcheck clean) with Raycast metadata (schemaVersion 1, mode silent, title Toggle MV7 Mute, an icon); calls the installed binary by absolute path; prints a one-line HUD message (Muted / Unmuted) and on failure prints the error and exits non-zero so Raycast shows it; integrations/raycast/README.md explains adding the folder as a Raycast Script Directory and assigning the Hyper+M hotkey; the maintainer confirms the hotkey toggles the mic from any app.

title: Map a Moonlander key to Hyper+M in Oryx
description: the maintainer does this in Oryx (configure.zsa.io) and flashes with Keymapp. The agent's role: give exact Oryx steps (assign a key with all four modifiers + M, or Oryx's Hyper modifier option with M) and help debug if the hotkey does not fire (Raycast hotkey conflicts, macOS keyboard shortcut conflicts).
acceptance_criteria: A Moonlander key (layer and position the maintainer picks) sends Cmd+Ctrl+Opt+Shift+M; firmware flashed with Keymapp; pressing it toggles the MV7 mute from any app; the key position is noted on this issue (do not paste the Oryx layout link: it is personal).

title: Keep upstream's release workflow from running on the fork
description:
Actions are enabled on the fork. release-plz.yml is already guarded by `github.repository_owner == 'Justkant'`, but release.yml runs on any pushed v* tag and would build and publish a cargo-dist release on the fork. Until then the rule in AGENTS.md is: never push v* tags to origin.

Prefer `gh workflow disable release.yml --repo johndturn/mv7mute` (no diff against upstream) over editing the file; confirm with the maintainer since it changes GitHub settings.
acceptance_criteria: release.yml cannot publish a GitHub release from johndturn/mv7mute (owner guard like release-plz.yml's, or the workflow disabled for the fork via gh workflow disable); CI (ci.yml) still runs; decision recorded in AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Removed release.yml and release-plz.yml from the fork (personal fork, no releases). ci.yml stays. On upstream syncs, resolve modify/delete conflicts on these files by keeping the deletion.

title: Add dependency audit (cargo-audit or cargo-deny) to the verify routine
description: The review checked the dependency tree by hand (23 crates for the CLI, all crates.io with lockfile checksums). An automated RustSec advisory check makes upstream syncs safer. cargo-audit is the smaller step; cargo-deny also covers licenses and sources. Local only; no need to add it to CI.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen tool installed (cargo install --locked), run once with results noted here; /verify command and the verifier subagent run it; AGENTS.md commands table updated.

title: Toggle can act on a stale micMute event
description: get_mute sends `micMute` then takes the first IN report containing micMute=on/off. The device also sends unsolicited `micMute=%s` events when the pad is touched. If an event is queued when the query is sent, toggle could invert the wrong state. Low likelihood (hidapi only buffers reports received since open), but cheap to harden.
acceptance_criteria: Before sending a query (micMute, lock), pending input reports are drained (short non-blocking reads) so the reply read is the reply to this query; covered by a unit test with the mock transport; clippy/test pass.
